title: Debug Info Generation
concept: Debug info embeds source-level information in binaries — enabling debuggers to show source code, variables, and stack traces instead of assembly.
why: Without debug info, debugging means reading assembly. With debug info, you see your source code, variable names, and values — the difference is productivity vs frustration.
theory:
## From Binary to Source Code

### Debug Info Formats

| Platform | Format | Tools |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Linux | DWARF | GDB, LLDB, Valgrind |
| macOS | DWARF (dSYM) | LLDB, Instruments |
| Windows | PDB | WinDbg, Visual Studio |

### What Debug Info Contains

```
Binary without debug info:
  0x401000: 48 89 e5 48 83 ec 10 c7 45 fc 2a 00 00 00

Binary with debug info:
  0x401000: 48 89 e5 48 83 ec 10 c7 45 fc 2a 00 00 00
  → source: main.xi:5
  → variable: x at [rbp-4], type: Int, value: 42
```

### Debug Info Contents

- **Source file mapping**: Which binary instruction came from which source line
- **Variable locations**: Where each variable lives (register, stack offset)
- **Type information**: Complete type definitions for all types
- **Function names**: Demangled names for all functions
- **Scope information**: When variables are alive/dead
- **Inline information**: In which function an inlined instruction originated

### Generating Debug Info

```sh
# Build with debug info
xiom build -g

# Full debug info (larger binary)
xiom build -g3

# No debug info (release builds)
xiom build --release  # Strips debug info by default
```

### Debugging Experience

```sh
# Launch debugger
lldb ./target/debug/myapp

(lldb) breakpoint set --name main
(lldb) run
(lldb) frame variable
(Int) x = 42
(Str) name = "Kilo"

(lldb) source list
  3    fn main() -> Int {
  4      let x = 42;
→ 5      let name = "Kilo";
  6      io.println(name);
  7      return x;
```

### Split Debug Info

```sh
# Linux: separate debug file
xiom build -g --split-debuginfo=packed
# Creates: myapp + myapp.dwp (debug info)

# macOS: dSYM bundle
xiom build -g
# Creates: myapp + myapp.dSYM/

# Windows: PDB file
xiom build -g --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# Creates: myapp.exe + myapp.pdb
```
syntax_ref:
xiom build -g                 # Include debug info
xiom build -g3                # Maximum debug info
xiom build --release           # No debug info (default)

# Debug:
lldb ./target/debug/myapp     # macOS
 gdb ./target/debug/myapp      # Linux
tips: Always build with -g during development — debug info is invaluable when things go wrong
Split debug info reduces binary size for deployment while keeping debugging capability
DWARF debug info can be very large — use -g1 for line info only, -g3 for full type info
lldb (macOS) and gdb (Linux) are your friends — learn basic breakpoint and inspection commands
common_mistakes: Building release without debug info and then trying to debug — you see assembly, not source
Not realizing debug info increases binary size 2-10x — split debug info for deployment
Assuming debug info captures everything — optimized code (-O2 with -g) may have variables optimized out
